newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates steady to firmer, paper yields up.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates steady to firmer, paper yields up.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady to firmer in moderate Tuesday trading with b orrowing interest in two-week to one-month money, dealers said.
Overnight cash rose to 4-15/16 7/8 percent from 4-7/8 3/4 and three-month money was steady at 5-7/16 5/16 percent.
"Two-week and one-month rates rose between 1/16 and 1/32 on Chinese New Year demand," one European bank dealer said, adding that trading was otherwise featureless.
Dealers expected demand on short-dated money to increase ahead of the New Year holidays starting in early February, but the upside on money rates was seen limited in a liquid market.

Trade in Exchange Fund bills and notes was relatively active with participants interested in taking six-month and one-year bills and longer-dated notes, dealers said. One week Exchange Fund bill yields rose to 4.43 percent from 4.38.
The yield on the three-year note was 6.22 percent versus 6.19, while five-year note yields edged up one point to 6.66 percent. Seven-year was at 6.89 percent versus 6.88.
Traders differed on the immediate prospect for U.S. treasuries since the U.S. 30-year bond seemed stuck around a yield of 6.83 percent.
